text:
zara: quick follow-up on rollout metadata shape: I'm proposing we add 'cohort_priority' (ordered list) + a compact lease string format (ttl=3600;hb=true) so resolvers can deterministically pick which cohort wins when overlaps happen.

mike: show an example?

zara: tiny sketch: cohort_priority= ["canary", "region-us", "global"], rollout= [{cohort:canary,pct:5},{cohort:region-us,pct:60}], lease:"ttl=3600;hb=true"; alert_refs:["ap-21"] ; fallback: redwood/gptx-6b@v1

olga: ordering makes sense. prefer explicit precedence doc: customer_pin > cohort_priority > rollout_percent > resolver_default. also vote to make cohort names canonical (no spaces) to avoid parsing issues in Dedicated.

ben: ops note: when an auto action (soft_unpin/unpin) happens, runtime should emit an audit pointer 'audit_ref' and a short reason code (e.g., "ALERT_TRIGGERED", "LEASE_EXPIRED"). metadata stays small; audits carry the details.

zara: agree. add reconcile_hint_secs to the schema so dedicated clusters know how long to wait before forcing convergence after a change. default 600.

mike: SDK compatibility: keep lease as a string to avoid breaking older clients. we'll parse server-side. Also ensure alert_refs is a list of strings only.

olga: small validation rule: pct sums per co-located cohorts shouldn't exceed 100. add server-side check and reject invalid rollout writes.

ops-bot: NOTICE: rollout accepted for redwood/gptx-6b@v1 by zara at 3799998888. cohorts: canary(5%), region-us(60%).

ben: I'll draft the audit-event schema (audit_ref, reason_code, model_id, rollout_id, fallback_ref) and a short runbook for operators.

zara: thanks — I'll add the compact schema + precedence table to the RFC and include parsing examples for Dedicated/Private. tagging you all when PR is ready. :white_check_mark:
